perspective:
Keith Ndiaye’s available information:

- He is a construction worker at a construction company; Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist there. They have a friendly but professional colleague relationship, often interacting when Keith visits the office for paperwork and project updates.
- Recently, Keith noticed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him and seeming off. He wondered if he had unknowingly upset her through a misunderstanding or mistake.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, not at all, and that she was dealing with personal stuff, apologizing if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He told her he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Keith heard Elizabeth share more about her stresses, which seemed severe to him. He suggested she consider talking to a professional for an external perspective. Elizabeth replied that she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth becoming slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful. He told her he hoped he had not overstepped and that he was there to support her. Elizabeth said he had not overstepped, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- After their last conversation, Keith perceived Elizabeth as more open and appreciative of his concern. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He intended to maintain a supportive relationship.
- Keith told Elizabeth he was glad they could talk and that he was always available if she needed to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot to her, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
